VIGIL —

Vulnerability-Adaptive In-Core Guarded Instruction Lane · Selective temporal checking on BOOMv3.

Chipyard · SonicBOOM · RV64GCFull M0 regression: not cleared
01 / Motivation
02 / Mechanism
03 / Current evidence
04 / The blocker

Why this question?

Temporal redundancy can detect some transient faults by comparing work performed at different times. Duplicating every instruction costs resources; checking only vulnerable work could reduce that cost, if the classification and recovery mechanisms are correct.

Proposed mechanism

The current specification describes a four-class AVF classifier, a single-issue shadow lane, commit-time comparison, and hybrid branch/fault-checkpoint recovery. It defines a minimum ROB extension and an eight-entry checkpoint ring.

Core research question: can selective checking lower the cost of temporal redundancy without making error coverage or recovery unreliable?

What has been tested

Earlier isolated checker tests passed: the JAL checker unit was 7/7 and the comparator unit was 2/2. These are unit checks only. They do not establish that the BOOM integration is correct.

What is not yet established

The M0 regression is not cleared. A previous run encountered an ELF/runtime mismatch, and the latest runtime status remains inconclusive. There is no completed end-to-end reliability result to claim yet.

Next gate

Reproduce the pinned RV64GC baseline, resolve the mismatch, clear the regression, and then compare the guarded design against an unmodified baseline under controlled fault injections. Only then can coverage, timing and area trade-offs be reported.
